newsitem.title: USA: Renoir bather sold in New York for $12.4 million.
newsitem.headline: Renoir bather sold in New York for $12.4 million.

text.p: An oil painting of a red-haired girl bathing by Pierre Auguste Renoir sold for $12.4 million in a sale of impressionist and modern painting and sculpture at Christie's auction house on Wednesday night.
An anonymous buyer decided the 1888 work was worth more than its estimate of $8 million to $10 million.
Eyes averted, the girl in "Young Woman Bathing" demurely shields her body with her hands in a pose that alludes to several classical paintings and sculptures.

The work was the most expensive item in the $119.8 million evening sale. The total fell within its estimated range of $102 million to $137 million, although several important works failed to meet the minimum price required for a sale.
Bidding on a 1888 ink drawing of a flower garden by Vincent van Gogh stopped at $7 million. The work, which sold for $8.3 million in 1990, was expected to bring $10 million.

Van Gogh started the series to which the drawing belongs in an effort to cut costs, since he could not afford canvas and paints. "I believe it's possible to produce a work of art at less cost than one must spend on a painting," he wrote his brother, the Christie's catalogue said.

An American private collector bought Claude Monet's "The Seine in Argenteuil" for $8.3 million, slightly above estimates. The 1875 landscape includes strollers, a sailboat and a small village in the distance.
Christopher Burge, chairman of Christie's New York, said the "positively triumphant" sales results reflected a strong but not irrational market.
